title: Number of connected components
label: idb-list
statement: You have `n` nodes and a list of undirected edges. Return **how many connected components** there are — groups of nodes that can reach each other.
provenance: **InterviewDB-listed.** LeetCode 323 is on the LinkedIn list you supplied from InterviewDB. No candidate report of this exact question was found in the research passes — the evidence is that the list names it. On that list it uses the same pattern as InterviewDB Q2. Q2 fails on hidden components if you only walk from one start node, which is the mistake 323 is designed to catch. Same outer loop over every unvisited vertex.

learn.title: 1 · Problem
learn.md: You have `n` nodes and a list of undirected edges. Return **how many connected components** there are — groups of nodes that can reach each other.

learn.title: 2 · Clarifications
learn.md:
- Can edges repeat or form cycles? (Yes — handle both.)
- Isolated nodes count as their own component? (Yes.)

learn.title: 3 · Key insight
learn.md: Start with n groups. Each edge that joins two **different** groups merges them, so the count drops by one. Union-find tracks which group each node is in, in near-constant time per edge.

learn.title: 4 · Approach
learn.md: I would say, before coding: "S."tart with n groups and let union-find merge across each edge; only edges between different groups lower the count — O((n + e) α(n))."

learn.title: 12 · Common AI mistakes
learn.md:
- Counting every edge as a merge (cycles and duplicates would over-count).
- Recursive DFS overflowing on a 300,000-node chain.
- Forgetting isolated nodes.
